title: Retail Lighting Design Study
description: A retail lighting design study developed to explore how lighting composition can influence the perception of spaciousness and closure within a sales environment. The project applied John Flynn’s psychological lighting principles while addressing visual performance, customer experience, energy use, glare control, and the needs of retail personnel.
description2: Two contrasting lighting scenes were developed. The spaciousness scene used higher-intensity, more uniform illumination together with peripheral wall lighting to create an open and energetic environment. The closure scene used lower-intensity, non-uniform lighting with reduced peripheral illumination to create a more intimate atmosphere. Track lighting, 2' × 2' panel luminaires, cove lighting, accent lighting, and task lighting were integrated into the overall design strategy.
overview: The study examined how lighting intensity, distribution, contrast, peripheral illumination, and layered lighting strategies could be used to create two distinct psychological impressions within the same retail environment.

objectives.title: Spaciousness
objectives.description: The spaciousness scene used higher-intensity, more uniform illumination together with peripheral wall lighting to create a brighter, more open, and visually expansive retail environment.

objectives.title: Closure
objectives.description: The closure scene used lower-intensity, non-uniform lighting with reduced peripheral illumination to create a more intimate and visually contained atmosphere.

strategies.title: Ambient Lighting
strategies.description: 2' × 2' panel luminaires provided the principal ambient illumination and established the general lighting level throughout the space.

strategies.title: Accent and Display Lighting
strategies.description: Track lighting was used to highlight merchandise, strengthen visual hierarchy, and create contrast between displays and surrounding areas.

strategies.title: Cove and Peripheral Lighting
strategies.description: Cove and peripheral lighting were used selectively to reinforce spatial perception, particularly in the spaciousness scene.

performance.title: Illuminance and Uniformity
performance.description: Horizontal illumination and distribution were evaluated to support retail activity, circulation, displays, and visual tasks.

performance.title: Visual Comfort
performance.description: Luminaire placement, brightness, contrast, and potential glare were considered in relation to customer and employee comfort.

performance.title: Energy and Sustainability
performance.description: Lighting power, luminaire selection, and system efficiency were considered as part of the design evaluation.

performance.title: Color Quality
performance.description: Color rendering and appearance were considered to support merchandise presentation.

performance.title: Staff Lighting Needs
performance.description: The design considered the needs of sales personnel who may spend extended periods within the retail environment.

performance.title: Task Lighting
performance.description: Counter and transaction areas were considered separately to provide suitable illumination for visual tasks.

highlights: Studied spaciousness and closure in retail environments
Integrated ambient, accent, display, cove, and counter lighting
Evaluated illuminance, uniformity, color rendering, energy use, and glare
Considered biological lighting needs for retail personnel
Applied applicable lighting criteria and design standards

title: Sustainable Outdoor Parking Lot Lighting Study
alt: Sustainable outdoor parking lot lighting study cover
description: An outdoor lighting design study focused on developing a sustainable parking-lot lighting system that balances visibility, uniformity, energy performance, and light-pollution control. The project evaluated the lighting design against IES RP-8-22, LEED light-pollution criteria, ANSI/ASHRAE/IES 90.1, and IDA/IES Model Lighting Ordinance guidance.
description2: The study covered an approximately 660' × 352' parking area and used GLN Galleon II luminaires from Cooper Lighting Solutions. The proposed layout incorporated approximately 60-foot horizontal and 57-foot vertical spacing between poles. A parametric analysis was also completed to evaluate how mounting height influenced average illuminance, maximum illuminance, uniformity, and vertical illuminance.
overview: The project explored how pole spacing, luminaire distribution, mounting height, and fixture selection influence parking-lot visibility, uniformity, energy performance, and light trespass.

objectives.title: Visibility and Uniformity
objectives.description: The design sought to provide appropriate illumination across the parking area while maintaining a balanced distribution and avoiding excessive bright and dark zones.

objectives.title: Light Pollution Control
objectives.description: Luminaire distribution and site-edge performance were evaluated to reduce unnecessary spill light and support light-pollution objectives.

strategies.title: Luminaire Selection
strategies.description: GLN Galleon II luminaires from Cooper Lighting Solutions were used to support the required site distribution and outdoor-lighting performance.

strategies.title: Pole Layout
strategies.description: The proposed layout used approximately 60-foot horizontal and 57-foot vertical pole spacing across the site.

strategies.title: Mounting Height Study
strategies.description: A parametric comparison was performed to evaluate how changes in pole height affected average illuminance, maximum illuminance, uniformity, and vertical illuminance.

performance.title: Horizontal Illuminance
performance.description: Average and maximum horizontal illuminance were evaluated across the parking area.

performance.title: Uniformity
performance.description: Lighting distribution was reviewed to evaluate the balance between minimum and average illuminance.

performance.title: Vertical Illuminance
performance.description: Vertical illuminance was evaluated to better understand visibility and spill-light conditions around the site.

performance.title: Pole Height
performance.description: The analysis showed that increasing mounting height reduced average and maximum illuminance while improving uniformity.

performance.title: Light Trespass
performance.description: Site-edge lighting conditions were reviewed in relation to light-pollution and boundary-control criteria.

performance.title: Energy Performance
performance.description: Fixture selection and system configuration were considered in relation to overall lighting efficiency.

highlights: Evaluated sustainability, visibility, uniformity, and light trespass
Performed a parametric study of pole mounting height
Reviewed horizontal and vertical illuminance performance
Applied IES RP-8-22 and light-pollution criteria
projectNotice: This project was completed as academic design work and is presented to demonstrate outdoor-lighting design, simulation, performance evaluation, and standards-based analysis. It is not presented as a commissioned HaSolantia client project.

title: Office Renovation Lighting Concept
alt: Office renovation architectural lighting concept cover
description: A competition lighting concept developed for the renovation of the first floor of a five-story office building in Sydney. The project addressed vestibules, general and executive lobbies, corridors, a lounge, and a multipurpose room while developing a cohesive lighting identity across spaces with different functional and experiential requirements.
description2: The lighting concept explored the relationship between daylight and electric lighting to create smoother transitions throughout the interior environment. Public areas such as lobbies and the multipurpose room used brighter and more uniform ambient lighting to reinforce spaciousness, while corridors and lounge spaces used lower ambient levels and more non-uniform distribution to support a calmer atmosphere. The design incorporated ambient, task, linear, accent, and architectural lighting strategies.
overview: The project developed a unified architectural-lighting concept for multiple first-floor office spaces while responding to different functional, visual, and experiential requirements.

objectives.title: Cohesive Lighting Identity
objectives.description: The design aimed to create one consistent lighting language across vestibules, lobbies, corridors, lounge areas, and the multipurpose room.

objectives.title: Spatial Experience
objectives.description: Different lighting intensities and distributions were used to reinforce spaciousness in public zones and create calmer, more intimate conditions in circulation and lounge areas.

strategies.title: Daylight Integration
strategies.description: The concept explored transitions between available daylight and electric lighting to create a continuous visual experience.

strategies.title: Layered Lighting
strategies.description: Ambient, task, linear, accent, and architectural lighting were combined to address both functional and experiential requirements.

strategies.title: Architectural Emphasis
strategies.description: Lighting was used to reinforce artwork, architectural surfaces, circulation paths, and focal elements within the renovated spaces.

performance.title: Ambient Lighting
performance.description: Public spaces such as lobbies and the multipurpose room used brighter and more uniform ambient lighting.

performance.title: Visual Atmosphere
performance.description: Corridors and lounge areas used lower ambient levels and more non-uniform distribution to create a calmer atmosphere.

performance.title: Functional Lighting
performance.description: Task and circulation requirements were considered alongside the broader architectural concept.

performance.title: Architectural Integration
performance.description: Lighting elements were integrated with architectural features and interior surfaces to support a unified design language.

highlights: Focused on office renovation and architectural lighting identity
Included vestibules, lobbies, corridors, lounge, and multipurpose spaces
Developed rendered views, lighting plans, fixture schedules, and concept imagery
Used layered ambient, task, linear, and accent lighting approaches
projectNotice: This project was developed as an IES Brandston competition submission and is presented as conceptual design work rather than commissioned HaSolantia client work.
